_comment: Public copy of the shipped config. THREE gates to send live: dry_run:false AND template_approved:true AND real copy in every template. This copy ships with the first two OFF and a placeholder identity — set them deliberately. Sourcing is headless via pipeline/apollo_pull.py (Apollo REST key in ~/.config/<campaign>/apollo.env).
_identity_note: from_address/reply_to must be the mailbox the OAuth token belongs to. If you run two campaigns off one address, give each its own token directory and never run both at once: each counts its daily cap from its own send log, so concurrent runs stack on one sending reputation.
_domain_note: One send per company domain, ever. Identical copy landing on several mailboxes in one corporate tenant is what trips a shared spam filter. Freemail is exempt.
_breaker_note: 5% (vs the sibling campaign's 6%) because Apollo corporate email bounces harder than commit-history addresses. Burst stays [4,10]: [3,10] false-trips across overlapping windows. NOTE the signal is censored - M365/Workspace quarantine returns no NDR, so the breaker cannot see spam-foldering.
_schedule_note: Follow-the-sun is emergent, not scripted: tz_scheduler mails everyone at 08:00-11:00 THEIR local time, so EU sends overnight for a US-based operator and the Americas follow through the morning. zone_quota then caps each UTC-offset bucket's share of the daily cap -- eu_share splits 50/50 between Europe and the Americas, then evenly across the zones with supply. A region that cannot fill its budget donates the slack, so fairness never costs volume.
_breaker_disabled_note: The automatic halt ships disabled. Bounces are still scanned and hard-bounced addresses are still suppressed, and the rate stays on the dashboard - only the automatic stop is off, because a binary halt false-trips on small windows (see _throttle_note). Set breaker_enabled true to restore it. Whichever you choose, do not run a cold stream with no brake at all.
_throttle_note: Bounce rate scales the daily cap instead of flipping a halt: >=4% -> 75%, >=7% -> 50%, >=12% -> 25%, >=20% -> stop. Below throttle_min_n sends in the window the rate is noise and the cap stays full -- the binary breaker fired on 3/28 (95% CI ~2-28%) and stopped the campaign for nothing. Reputation harm scales with volume, so throttling is the proportionate response; only a genuinely bad list reaches zero.
_verify_note: Bouncer mailbox verification, run by pipeline/verify_queue.py as its own chain step before the send. OFF until the one-off pass over the existing queue is reviewed by hand. Only 'undeliverable' is terminal; risky / unknown / deliverable-on-an-accept-all-domain are recorded and stay sendable so the harder rules get set from real bounce outcomes. See method/VERIFY-PLAN.md.
_verify_cull_note: Hosts thrown out pre-send WITHOUT a Bouncer call. 2026-07-21: Mimecast and Barracuda bounced heavily in this campaign's own data. Both are secure email gateways that quarantine silently and return no NDR, so the throttle can never catch them -- pre-send is the only place. Bouncer only ever abstained on them. Reversible: empty the list to send them again.
